questionText: 8²+15²=x². Find x.
hints: A small 2 above a number means multiply the number by itself. Work out the left side first, then find the number whose square matches it.
Find 8 × 8 and 15 × 15 and add them. Then look for a number that gives that total when it is multiplied by itself.
Similar example: 6² + 8² = n². 6 × 6 = 36 and 8 × 8 = 64, and 36 + 64 = 100. Since 10 × 10 = 100, n is 10.

stepByStep.text: Square 8.
Square 15.
Add the two squares.
Find the number that multiplies by itself to make 289. So x is 17.

misconceptions.A: This adds 8 and 15 without squaring them. Square each number first, then add.
misconceptions.C: 25 × 25 = 625, which is far too big. The two squares add up to 289.
misconceptions.D: 15 is already one of the numbers in the sum. x must be bigger, because x times x is 225 with 64 more added.

Find 5 × 5 and 12 × 12 and add them. Then look for a number that gives that total when it is multiplied by itself.
Similar example: 3² + 4² = n². 3 × 3 = 9 and 4 × 4 = 16, and 9 + 16 = 25. Since 5 × 5 = 25, n is 5.

stepByStep.text: Square 5.
Square 12.
Add the two squares.
Find the number that multiplies by itself to make 169. So M is 13.

misconceptions.B: This is 12 take away 5. Square each number first, then add the squares.
misconceptions.C: 169 is M times M. The question asks for M itself, the number that multiplies by itself to make 169.
misconceptions.D: 12 is already one of the numbers in the sum. M must be bigger, because M times M is 144 with 25 more added.

questionText: Chairs in rows = chairs in columns. Hall filled. Number of men?
hints: When the number of rows equals the number of chairs in each row, the chairs make a square. Think about what kind of number the total must be.
The total is a number multiplied by itself. Test each choice: can it be written as some number times that same number?

Similar example: could a hall like this hold 196 people? Yes, because 14 × 14 = 196, so there are 14 rows of 14 chairs. Could it hold 200? No, because 200 lies between 14 × 14 = 196 and 15 × 15 = 225.

stepByStep.text: The rows and columns are equal, so the number of chairs is a number times itself. It must be a square number.
Try 18 rows of 18 chairs.
The other choices are not squares. 131 lies between 121 and 144, 275 lies between 256 and 289, and 325 is one more than 324.
Only 324 is a square number. So the number of men is 324.

misconceptions.A: 11 × 11 = 121 and 12 × 12 = 144. 131 falls between them, so it cannot fill equal rows and columns.
misconceptions.B: This is very close, but 18 × 18 = 324. 325 is one too many to make a square.
misconceptions.C: 16 × 16 = 256 and 17 × 17 = 289. 275 falls between them, so it is not a square number.
misconceptions.D: Yes! 18 rows of 18 chairs make 18 × 18 = 324.

questionText: Sum of which pair gives square number?
hints: A square number is a number times itself, like 49 or 100. Add each pair and see which total is a square number.
Start by adding the first pair, 91 and 19. Then check whether the total sits exactly on a square, such as 10 × 10 or 11 × 11.
Similar example: is 87 + 57 a square number? 87 + 57 = 144, and 12 × 12 = 144, so yes. Is 60 + 30 a square? 60 + 30 = 90, which lies between 9 × 9 = 81 and 10 × 10 = 100, so no.

stepByStep.text: Add the first pair. 110 lies between 100 and 121, so it is not a square.
Add the second pair.
225 is a square number.
The other two pairs give 59 + 52 = 111 and 76 + 78 = 154. Neither is a square number.
So the pair whose sum is a square number is 157 & 68.

misconceptions.A: 91 + 19 = 110. That lies between 10 × 10 = 100 and 11 × 11 = 121, so it is not a square.
misconceptions.C: 59 + 52 = 111. That lies between 10 × 10 = 100 and 11 × 11 = 121, so it is not a square.
misconceptions.D: 76 + 78 = 154. That lies between 12 × 12 = 144 and 13 × 13 = 169, so it is not a square.

Find 29 × 29 for the left side. For the right side, find 31 × 31 and 10 × 10, then subtract.
Similar example: compare 12² with 13² − 6². The left side is 12 × 12 = 144. On the right, 13 × 13 = 169 and 6 × 6 = 36, and 169 − 36 = 133. 144 is more than 133, so the sign is >.

stepByStep.text: Work out the left side.
On the right side, square 31.
Square 10 to get 100, and subtract it.
841 is smaller than 861, so the left side is less than the right side. The sign is <.

misconceptions.A: Yes! The left side is 841 and the right side is 861, so the left side is smaller.
misconceptions.B: Check the right side. 31 × 31 = 961, and taking away 100 leaves 861, which is more than 841.
misconceptions.C: The two sides are close but not equal. The left side is 841 and the right side is 861.
misconceptions.D: One of the signs does fit. Work out both sides: 841 on the left and 861 on the right.

questionText: Greatest number: 28 multiplied by to get perfect square?
hints: A perfect square is a number times itself. Try each choice and see whether the product is a perfect square.
Break 28 into small factors: 4 × 7 = 28. The 4 is already a square, 2 × 2. Think about what the lonely 7 needs.
Similar example: what should 12 be multiplied by to get a perfect square? 4 × 3 = 12. The 4 is a square but the 3 has no partner. Multiply by 3: 12 × 3 = 36, and 6 × 6 = 36.

stepByStep.text: Break 28 into factors. 4 is already a square, but 7 has no partner.
Give 7 a partner by multiplying by 7.
Check that 196 is a perfect square.
So 28 must be multiplied by 7.

misconceptions.A: 28 × 12 = 336. That lies between 18 × 18 = 324 and 19 × 19 = 361, so it is not a perfect square.
misconceptions.B: 28 × 10 = 280. That lies between 16 × 16 = 256 and 17 × 17 = 289, so it is not a perfect square.
misconceptions.D: 28 × 5 = 140. That lies between 11 × 11 = 121 and 12 × 12 = 144, so it is not a perfect square.

questionText: Sum of squares of which two gives square?
hints: Square each number in a pair, add the two squares, and see whether the total is itself a square number.
Start with the first pair: find 10 × 10 and 15 × 15 and add them. Then check if that total is some number times itself.
Similar example: 9 and 12. 9 × 9 = 81 and 12 × 12 = 144, and 81 + 144 = 225. Since 15 × 15 = 225, the sum of the squares is a square number.

stepByStep.text: Try 10 and 15. 325 is one more than 18 times 18, so it is not a square.
Try 7 and 24. Square each and add.
625 is a square number.
The other two pairs give 64 + 2025 = 2089 and 81 + 625 = 706. Neither is a square number.
So the pair is 7 and 24.

misconceptions.A: 100 + 225 = 325. That is just one more than 18 × 18 = 324, so it is not a square.
misconceptions.C: 64 + 2025 = 2089. That lies between 45 × 45 = 2025 and 46 × 46 = 2116, so it is not a square.
misconceptions.D: 81 + 625 = 706. That lies between 26 × 26 = 676 and 27 × 27 = 729, so it is not a square.

questionText: Least number by which 588 should be multiplied to make a perfect square?
hints: A perfect square is made of factors that all come in pairs. Break 588 into small factors and look for one without a partner.
Start dividing 588 by 2, then by 2 again, and keep going with small prime numbers. Write 588 as a product of primes.
Similar example: 180. Its prime factors are 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 5 = 180. The 2s pair up and the 3s pair up, but 5 is alone. Multiply by 5: 180 × 5 = 900, and 30 × 30 = 900.

stepByStep.text: Break 588 into prime factors.
The two 2s make a pair and the two 7s make a pair. The 3 has no partner.
Multiply by 3 to give it a partner.
Check that 1764 is a perfect square.
The least number is 3, which is not among the numbers given. So the answer is None of these.

misconceptions.A: 588 × 2 = 1176. The 2s already had partners and the 3 is still alone, so this is not a square.
misconceptions.B: 588 × 6 = 3528. This gives the 3 a partner but leaves an extra 2 alone, so it is not a square.
misconceptions.C: 588 × 4 = 2352. The 3 still has no partner, so this is not a square.
misconceptions.D: Yes! The lonely factor is 3, and 3 is not listed, so none of the numbers given fits.

questionText: What number added to 1234 gives a square number?
hints: Find the square numbers that sit close to 1234. The number to add is the gap up to a square above it.
Try 35 × 35 and 36 × 36. See which one is just above 1234.
Similar example: what must be added to 380 to get a square number? 19 × 19 = 361 is too small, and 20 × 20 = 400 is the next square. 400 − 380 = 20, so add 20.

stepByStep.text: 35 times 35 is a little less than 1234.
So the next square above 1234 is 36 times 36.
Find the gap from 1234 up to 1296. The number to add is 62.

misconceptions.A: 1234 + 45 = 1279. That lies between 35 × 35 = 1225 and 36 × 36 = 1296, so it is not a square.
misconceptions.B: 1234 + 25 = 1259. That lies between 35 × 35 = 1225 and 36 × 36 = 1296, so it is not a square.
misconceptions.C: 1234 + 57 = 1291. That is close, but the next square is 36 × 36 = 1296.

questionText: Sum of which two numbers gives a square? 159&165, 198&145, 189&330, none
hints: A square number is a number times itself, like 49 or 100. Add each pair and see which total is a square number.
Start by adding the first pair, 159 and 165. Then check whether the total is some number times itself. Try numbers near 18.
Similar example: is 130 + 126 a square number? 130 + 126 = 256, and 16 × 16 = 256, so yes. Is 75 + 50 a square? 75 + 50 = 125, which lies between 11 × 11 = 121 and 12 × 12 = 144, so no.

stepByStep.text: Add the first pair.
324 is a square number.
The other pairs give 198 + 145 = 343 and 189 + 330 = 519. Neither is a square number.
So the pair whose sum is a square is 159 and 165.

misconceptions.B: 198 + 145 = 343. That lies between 18 × 18 = 324 and 19 × 19 = 361, so it is not a square.
misconceptions.C: 189 + 330 = 519. That lies between 22 × 22 = 484 and 23 × 23 = 529, so it is not a square.
misconceptions.D: One pair does work. Add 159 and 165, then compare the total with 18 × 18.

questionText: Quotient: smallest 4-digit square ÷ greatest 2-digit even square?
hints: There are two numbers to find before dividing: the smallest square with 4 digits, and the biggest even square with 2 digits.
For the first number, try 31 × 31 and 32 × 32 and see which one first reaches 4 digits. For the second, list the 2-digit squares and pick the biggest even one.

Similar example: divide the smallest 3-digit square by the greatest 1-digit even square. 10 × 10 = 100 is the smallest 3-digit square. The 1-digit squares are 1, 4 and 9, so the greatest even one is 4. 100 ÷ 4 = 25.

stepByStep.text: 31 times 31 has only 3 digits.
So the smallest 4-digit square is 32 times 32.
The 2-digit squares are 16, 25, 36, 49, 64 and 81. The greatest even one is 64.
Divide. The quotient is 16.

misconceptions.A: Check the two numbers first. The smallest 4-digit square is 32 × 32 = 1024, and the greatest 2-digit even square is 8 × 8 = 64.
misconceptions.B: Remember the 2-digit square must be even. 81 is bigger but odd, so use 64, then divide 1024 by it.
misconceptions.C: This is close. Work out 1024 ÷ 64 again. It helps to know that 64 × 10 = 640.
misconceptions.D: Yes! The two squares are 1024 and 64, and 1024 ÷ 64 = 16.

questionText: Remainder when greatest 2-digit square divided by smallest 2-digit square?
hints: First find the two square numbers the question describes. Then divide the bigger by the smaller and see what is left over.
List the squares that have 2 digits, starting from 4 × 4. The first one in your list and the last one are the two numbers you need.

Similar example: find the remainder when the greatest 3-digit square is divided by the smallest 3-digit square. They are 31 × 31 = 961 and 10 × 10 = 100. Nine 100s make 900, and 961 − 900 = 61. The remainder is 61.

stepByStep.text: The 2-digit squares are 16, 25, 36, 49, 64 and 81. The greatest is 81 and the smallest is 16.
See how many 16s fit into 81. Five of them fit.
Find what is left over. The remainder is 1.

misconceptions.A: Check which squares you used. The greatest 2-digit square is 81 and the smallest is 16.
misconceptions.B: Yes! 5 × 16 = 80, and 81 is just 1 more than 80.
misconceptions.C: This is what is left when 100 is divided by 16, but 100 has 3 digits. The greatest 2-digit square is 81.
misconceptions.D: Check the two squares: 81 and 16. Five 16s make 80, so see how much of 81 is left.

questionText: Find the odd one out: 144, 169, 196, 256, 324, 400
hints: All the numbers look alike in one way, so look for a second property that one number does not share.
Find which number each one is the square of. Then look at whether each number is even or odd.
Similar example: 9, 25, 36, 49, 81. These are the squares of 3, 5, 6, 7 and 9. All of them are odd except 36, so 36 is the odd one out.

stepByStep.text: These are all square numbers: the squares of 12, 13, 14, 16, 18 and 20.
144, 196, 256, 324 and 400 are all even numbers.
169 is the square of 13, and it is an odd number.
So the odd one out is 169.

misconceptions.A: 144 is 12 × 12 and it is even, like most of the others. Look for the one number that is odd.
misconceptions.B: Yes! Every number here is a square, but 169 is the only odd one.
misconceptions.C: 196 is 14 × 14 and it is even, like most of the others. Look for the one number that is odd.
misconceptions.D: 324 is 18 × 18 and it is even, like most of the others. Look for the one number that is odd.

questionText: Which number does not belong to the group? 81, 121, 169, 289, 361, 529
hints: All the numbers look alike in one way, so look for a second property that one number does not share.
Find which number each one is the square of. Then ask what kind of numbers 11, 13, 17, 19 and 23 are.
Similar example: 4, 9, 25, 36, 49. These are the squares of 2, 3, 5, 6 and 7. All of those are prime except 6, because 2 × 3 = 6. So 36 does not belong.

stepByStep.text: These are the squares of 9, 11, 13, 17, 19 and 23.
11, 13, 17, 19 and 23 are prime numbers. Each can be divided only by 1 and itself.
9 is not prime, because it is 3 times 3.
So the number that does not belong is 81.

misconceptions.A: Yes! 81 is 9 × 9, and 9 is not prime. All the others are squares of prime numbers.
misconceptions.B: 529 is 23 × 23, and 23 is a prime number. Look for the square of a number that is not prime.
misconceptions.C: 121 is 11 × 11, and 11 is a prime number. Look for the square of a number that is not prime.
misconceptions.D: 289 is 17 × 17, and 17 is a prime number. Look for the square of a number that is not prime.
